edits.before: Meep-chip the contacts and collect the first chimes — the wanderer's ledger opens.
edits.after: At level 1 neither side has a full combo - dodge Sear and meep-poke to keep it even.

edits.before: Q threats begin: every wall adjacency is a stun audition.
edits.after: W-Q poke out-damages you the moment he hits level 2.

edits.before: Full kit: shrine the sustain, tunnel the angles, and Q the geometry.
edits.after: His low-cooldown Pillar of Flame keeps him ahead in the poke war at 3.

edits.before: Chime economy: collect on the move and return with meep upgrades — absence is investment.
edits.after: Brand's ranged Q-W-E burst keeps controlling the lane through levels 4 and 5 while you farm.

edits.before: Tempered Fate online — the map's biggest moments now have a stasis clause.
edits.after: Pyroclasm adds lethal bounced AoE burst at 6 that you can't out-trade.

edits.before: First item: the meeps chunk and the portals make your jungler ambidextrous.
edits.after: His first AP item keeps the W-Q-E poke rotation dominant over your meeps.

edits.before: Bait the answer, start the chain, and let your carry collect — engage trades are all-or-nothing; pick the all.
edits.after: Tempered Fate stases Brand mid-cast during objective fights - his Pyroclasm burst simply never lands.

edits.before: Engaging into a banked disengage — the chain that starts answered is a donation with intentions.
edits.after: Standing near his shrine range invites free Pillar of Flame chip - back off, don't linger.

edits.before: - Brand Sear (Stun): matchup-defining — Q only stuns the ablaze — after eating W or E, the stun line is the dodge. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep E Magical Journey banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: - Brand Sear (Stun): 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s cooldown - it only stuns ablaze targets, so eating W or E first is the dodge line. - Keep E Magical Journey banked for their best play. - His R (100/90/80s) is a fight decision, not a habit.

notes: The packet's own defects field already flagged this chart contradiction (5/7 stages to Brand vs a 52.24% Bard winrate) — that's expected: winning most of the level-by-level stages of a poke matchup is consistent with an overall near-even lane once Bard's R/E utility and late scaling pull it back, which phases[6]='Skill' (unchanged, already agreed) already reflects. diffRating/carryRating (7/10, 7.5/10 TRICKY) were left as-is since they already lean Brand-favored and are consistent with the corrected chart.
